prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError subclasses (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args was set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__ — which doesn't match UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) constructor signature, raising a TypeError on every unpickle. prs.title: fix(server): duplicate stdio fds to prevent closing real stdio
prs.author: superShen0916
prs.reason:
[llm pick] cluster primary for issue #1933: All 5 PRs show CI as unknown to me and I could not independently query GitHub in this session (gh CLI and WebFetch calls were both blocked by permissions), so I'm ranking on the two verifiable, stated facts: diff size and technical approach implied by title.

Approach: #2040, #2722, and #2734 read as "prevent/preserve the stream from closing" fixes — typically implemented by monkeypatching or guarding `.close()` on the wrapped stdio stream, which only stops *that* call site from closing the handle and can still be bypassed by anything touching the raw fd. #2737 and #2866 both explicitly use `os.dup`/fd duplication — the standard, more robust fix, since it hands anyio a genuinely separate file descriptor and leaves the real stdin/stdout fd untouched regardless of what closes the wrapper. Two independent authors converging on the same os.dup strategy is a good signal it's the technically correct approach here.

prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly runs json.loads on plain string arguments for parameters typed as a union including str (e.g. str | None), which can corrupt a valid string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-serialized payload passed as a plain string). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly runs json.loads on plain string arguments for parameters typed as a union including str (e.g. str | None), which can corrupt a valid string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-serialized payload passed as a plain string). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same guard in pre_parse_json and fix the same str-union corruption bug, but take different-scoped approaches. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json skips pre-parsing for ANY union where all members are in a fixed {str,int,float,bool,None} set - this also disables pre-parsing for unions like str | int or str | bool, where json.loads is still the mechanism that coerces a numeric/bool-looking string into the non-str member; that's a behavior change beyond the reported bug and isn't covered by #2032's diff/tests shown. #3056 narrowly targets str | None (Optional[str]) specifically, matching the bug report's actual failure mode, and additionally unwraps Annotated[...] on individual union members (via _unwrap_annotated) so cases like `str | Annotated[int, Field(...)]` are handled correctly - a case #2032's diff does not address at all. #3056's narrower, better-justified scope (with an explanatory docstring on why other simple-type unions are intentionally left pre-parsed) makes it the safer fix to keep; #2032 should be closed as a duplicate/superseded fix.
